fixed_question: Intentional subject/Motion-class change (e.g. emissive flicker) vs unintended recolour?
observed_feature: Same figure silhouette wholesale-recoloured each frame with matching quantized palette shifts
rationale: Candidate and proposed_hard_fail_reference are the same strip. Across f0–f3 the subject and pose stay a pickaxe-bearing figure; only global colours change frame-to-frame. The required quantized_palette_histogram panel under each frame tracks that: blues/greens in f0, yellows/reds in f1, whites/purples in f2, darks/oranges in f3. That is unintended recolour / palette drift, not airborne-appropriate emissive flicker or a subject/motion-class change. Budget-binding good (16-moth-flap) keeps a stable beige/brown palette under motion, underscoring the contrast. Metric equals C (0.2793) at the hard-fail boundary with no caveats—valid hard-fail reference for palette_drift_pass.
